cues.en: Usually, I don't think notation in math matters that much. Don't get me wrong. I enjoy a bad notation rant as much as the next guy, and there are clearly a few simple changes to our conventions that could speed up learning for math students everywhere.
cues.zh: 通常，我觉得数学里的记号其实没那么重要。别误会我。我也很喜欢跟着大家一起吐槽糟糕的数学记号，而且显然只要对我们的常规做几个简单的改动，就能加快各地数学学生的学习速度。

cues.en: But at the end of the day, notation, good or bad, it's just not the point of math. Even the most carefully designed symbols and syntax will fail to capture the underlying visual that constitutes understanding.
cues.zh: 但归根结底，记号无论好坏，根本就不是数学的核心。即使是设计得再精妙的符号和语法，也无法捕捉到构成真正理解的那种底层直觉。

cues.en: I figured it's better to just spend time focusing on that underlying essence and let the symbols just be what they are in peace.
cues.zh: 我想，最好还是把时间花在关注这种底层本质上，让符号安安静话地做它们自己吧。

cues.en: But that said, when unintuitive notation actively stalls the gears of learning, my disposition on the matter hardens up a little bit. In particular, I'm thinking of one threesome of syntax, which when you stop and think about it, is an egregious source of friction in math education everywhere.
cues.zh: 话虽如此，当不直观的记号实实在在地阻碍了学习的齿轮时，我对这件事的态度就会变得强硬一点。特别是，我想到了由三个符号组成的语法组合，只要你停下来思考一下就会发现，它是各地数学教育中摩擦力的一个严重来源。

cues.en: If you take the fact that two multiplied by itself three times equals eight, for example, we have three separate ways to explain that relation
cues.zh: 举个例子，如果我们接受“2 自乘 3 次等于 8”这个事实，我们有三种不同的方式来解释这种关系

cues.en: Two cubed equals eight with a superscript.
cues.zh: 用上标表示 2 的 3 次方等于 8。

cues.en: The cube root of eight is two with a squaggly radical symbol,
cues.zh: 用一个弯弯曲曲的根号表示 8 的立方根是 2，

cues.en: and the log base two of eight equals three, which we write using the word log itself.
cues.zh: 以及以 2 为底 8 的对数等于 3，我们用 log 这个词本身来书写。

cues.en: What the hell do these three ways of writing the same fact have to do with each other? Making up syntax for a concept is fine, but don't do it in three completely different ways for the same concept and force students to learn every rule about that concept three separate times. It's like it's a different language.
cues.zh: 这三种书写同一个事实的方式到底有什么关系？为一个概念发明语法没问题，但不要为同一个概念搞出三种完全不同的方式，然后强迫学生把那个概念的所有规则重复学三遍。这简直就像在学一门不同的语言。

cues.en: This way of writing things isn't just counterintuitive,
cues.zh: 这种书写方式不仅违背直觉，

cues.en: it's counter mathematical.
cues.zh: 而且有悖数学。

cues.en: Since rather than making seemingly different facts look the same, which is what math should do,
cues.zh: 数学本该让看似不同的事实显得相同，而这种写法却反其道而行之，

cues.en: it takes three facts which should obviously be the same and makes them look artificially different.
cues.zh: 它把三个本来显而易见应该相同的事实，变得看起来人为地不同。

cues.en: Just think about how confusing logarithms were the first time that you learned about them.
cues.zh: 想想你刚学对数时觉得有多困惑吧。

cues.en: This is, of course, a known issue, and the Internet has no shortage of people raising the same concern with suggestions for a better notation.
cues.zh: 这当然是个已知的问题，互联网上从不缺提出同样担忧并建议更好记号的人。

cues.en: But recently,
cues.zh: 但最近，

cues.en: I stumbled across a Math Exchange post with a suggestion so lovely, so symmetrical,
cues.zh: 我偶然看到一篇 Math Exchange 上的帖子，里面的建议如此精妙、如此对称，

cues.en: so utterly reasonable
cues.zh: 如此无可挑剔，

cues.en: that I just have to share it.
cues.zh: 以至于我不得不分享给大家。

cues.en: For a relationship like two cubed equals eight, take a triangle and write two in the lower left,
cues.zh: 对于像二的立方等于八这样的关系，画一个三角形，左下角写二，

cues.en: three on the top, and eight on the lower right.
cues.zh: 顶部写三，右下角写八。

cues.en: To express the operation two cubed, remove that bottom right corner.
cues.zh: 要表达二的立方这个运算，擦掉右下角。

cues.en: The symbol as a whole represents the value that should go in the missing corner.
cues.zh: 整个符号代表应该填入缺失角落的值。

cues.en: To express log base two of eight, which is asking the question two to the what equals eight, remove the top number. The symbol as a whole represents the value that should go in the missing corner.
cues.zh: 要表达以二为底八的对数，也就是在问二的几次方等于八，擦掉顶部的数字。整个符号代表应该填入缺失角落的值。

cues.en: To express the cube root of eight, which is saying what number to the third power equals eight, remove the bottom left corner. The symbol as a whole represents the value that should go in the missing corner.
cues.zh: 要表达八的立方根，也就是在说哪个数字的三次方等于八，擦掉左下角的数字。整个符号代表应该填入缺失角落的值。

cues.en: In other words, all three operations are completely symmetrically represented.
cues.zh: 换句话说，这三种运算的表示方式是完全对称的。

cues.en: This triangle deserves a name, and a friend of mine at Khan Academy decided that we should call it the triangle of power.
cues.zh: 这个三角形值得拥有一个名字，我在可汗学院的一位朋友决定我们应该叫它“幂次三角形”。

cues.en: The definition alone is mildly pleasing, but where it gets fun is when you see how much smoother all of the different operations become.
cues.zh: 光是这个定义就挺让人愉快的，但真正有趣的是，你会发现所有这些不同的运算变得多么顺畅。

cues.en: In our current notation,
cues.zh: 在我们目前的记法中，

cues.en: there are six different ways to express the various inverse operations.
cues.zh: 有六种不同的方式来表达各种逆运算。

cues.en: Most of these are memorized as separate entities,
cues.zh: 其中大部分都被当作独立的实体来死记硬背，

cues.en: some are rarely even talked about, and there's no discernible pattern even though all of them describe the same basic idea.
cues.zh: 有些甚至很少被讨论，而且看不出有什么明显的规律，尽管它们描述的都是同一个基本概念。

cues.en: But students still have to spend six times the effort to memorize each one, are six times more likely to make a mistake, and have six separate opportunities to decide math is dumb and boring and conducive to failure, and why don't I just go study art instead?
cues.zh: 但学生们仍然得花上六倍的精力去分别记住每一个，出错的几率高出六倍，并且有六次机会去认定数学既愚蠢又无趣、只会让人失败，为什么我不去学艺术呢？

cues.en: With the triangle of power, all these operations follow the same pattern.
cues.zh: 有了幂次三角形，所有这些运算都遵循相同的规律。

cues.en: Our brains are really good at picking up on patterns like this, and you can much more easily imagine a smooth mental image associated with the property.
cues.zh: 我们的大脑非常擅长捕捉这样的规律，你可以更容易地在脑海中构建出一个与该性质相关的流畅心智图景。

cues.en: There's even kind of an aesthetic pleasure to this, and who knows, maybe more of the artistically inclined students would look favorably upon math long enough to see just how valuable their intuitions really are in the science.
cues.zh: 这甚至带有一种美学上的愉悦，谁知道呢，也许会有更多倾向于艺术的学生愿意对数学多看一眼，从而认识到他们直觉科学中的真正价值。

cues.en: Let's take another property,
cues.zh: 再看另一个性质，

cues.en: like the idea that a to the x times a to the y equals a to the x plus y.
cues.zh: 比如 a 的 x 次方乘以 a 的 y 次方，等于 a 的 x 加 y 次方。

cues.en: The corresponding fact for logarithms is that log of x times y equals log of x plus log of y.
cues.zh: 对数对应的规律是 log(x·y) 等于 log(x) 加 log(y)。

cues.en: When you write this with the triangle of power, it's a little easier to see that both of these expressions are really saying the same thing.
cues.zh: 用幂三角来写，就更容易看出这两个式子其实在说同一件事。

cues.en: Remember, the symbol as a whole represents the number at the missing corner. So the top expression is saying that when you multiply two numbers that belong on the bottom right of the triangle, it corresponds with adding the numbers that belong to the top. But that's also what the lower is saying. When you multiply the numbers at the bottom right, it corresponds with adding numbers that belong to the top.
cues.zh: 记住，整个符号代表缺失那个角上的数。所以上面那个式子是说，把两个属于三角形右下角的数相乘，对应的是把属于顶部的数相加。下面那个式子也是这么说的。把右下角的数相乘，对应的是把属于顶部的数相加。

cues.en: To help students with this, you could draw inside of the triangle, saying that when the lower left is constant, the numbers at the top like to add, while the bottom right numbers like to multiply.
cues.zh: 为了帮学生理解，可以在三角形里面画一画，说明当左下角固定时，顶部的数喜欢相加，而右下角的数喜欢相乘。

cues.en: What about when a different corner stays constant, like the top?
cues.zh: 那如果换成另一个角固定呢，比如顶部？

cues.en: Well, in this case, you'd write a multiplication sign in both the bottom corners because with exponents and radicals, multiplication turns into multiplication.
cues.zh: 这种情况下，你要在两个底角都写上乘号，因为对指数和根式来说，乘法会变成乘法。

cues.en: The natural question that a student might ask from here is if there's an analogous rule for when the lower right stays constant.
cues.zh: 学生自然会问，那右下角固定时有没有类似的规则呢？

cues.en: There is. You have to introduce a new operation, which for the sake of this video, I'll call o plus, where a o plus b equals
cues.zh: 有的。你得引入一个新运算，为了这个视频，我把它叫做 o plus，其中 a o plus b 等于

cues.en: one over one over a plus one over b.
cues.zh: 一除以（一除以 a 加一除以 b）。

cues.en: This is not actually a ridiculous thing to introduce since it comes up in physics all the time, like when you're computing parallel resistance.
cues.zh: 这其实并不是一件荒谬的事，因为它在物理学中经常出现，比如你在计算并联电阻时。

cues.en: With that symbol, you could say that when the lower right number stays constant,
cues.zh: 有了这个符号，你就可以说，当右下角的数字保持不变时，

cues.en: the top numbers like to get o plus
cues.zh: 顶部的数字倾向于进行相加运算，

cues.en: and the bottom left numbers like to get multiplied.
cues.zh: 而左下角的数字倾向于进行相乘运算。

cues.en: This is actually a really nice connection between logarithms and roots, and it never gets discussed,
cues.zh: 这其实是指数和根式之间一个非常美妙的联系，却从来没人讨论过，

cues.en: probably because the notation isn't really conducive to asking the question.
cues.zh: 可能因为这种记号实在不利于引发这样的思考。

cues.en: I could go on and on here, showing a lot of other properties.
cues.zh: 我还可以接着讲下去，展示更多其他的性质。

cues.en: But honestly,
cues.zh: 但老实说，

cues.en: I think the best case I can make here is to encourage you to explore it for yourself. And notice that just about everything involving exponents, logs, or radicals becomes nicer when you use the triangle of power.
cues.zh: 我觉得我能给出的最好建议，就是鼓励你们自己去探索。并会发现，几乎所有涉及指数、对数或根式的内容，在使用幂之三角形时都会变得更美好。

cues.en: By the way, I hope that it goes without saying that in this perfect world,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，不用我说大家也知道，在这个理想的世界里，

cues.en: students wouldn't learn these operations purely from the symbols. They should still ask why it's true and why it doesn't follow a different pattern.
cues.zh: 学生不应该纯粹从符号来学习这些运算。他们仍然应该去探究为什么它是对的，以及为什么它不遵循另一种规律。

cues.en: But the point is that when the notation actually reflects the math, the questions that students are most naturally asking tend to be the ones that cut right into the essence of what's going on.
cues.zh: 但关键在于，当记号真正反映数学本质时，学生们最自然提出的问题，往往正是直击事物核心本质的问题。

cues.en: The asymmetries in the notation correspond with actual asymmetries in the numerical relationship a to the b equals c itself,
cues.zh: 记号中的不对称性，恰好对应着 $a$ 的 $b$ 次方等于 $c$ 这一数值关系本身真实存在的不对称性，

cues.en: not any artificial asymmetries of squiggles and words.
cues.zh: 而不是那些符号和文字带来的虚假不对称。

cues.en: When a student asks why the top likes to get added in one context, but o plus ed in another, the teacher can point out the property that reflecting the triangle reciprocates the top. And then they can start addressing where that fact comes from.
cues.zh: 当一个学生问，为什么“top”在一种情境下喜欢被加上去，而在另一种情境下却是“o 加 ed”，老师可以指出这样一个性质：把三角形翻折过来，会让“top” reciprocate。然后他们就可以开始解释这个事实从何而来。

cues.en: My sincere hope is that students don't learn by symbolic pattern, but by substantive reasoning and read derivation within their own heads. But the fact is, most of us do first learn things by symbolic manipulation.
cues.zh: 我真诚的希望是，学生不要靠符号模式来学习，而是靠实质性推理，并在自己的头脑中进行推导。但事实是，我们大多数人最初确实是通过符号操作来学习东西的。

cues.en: So when there's an opportunity to significantly speed up that process, we should take it. And if you agree with me that the triangle of power is clearly better than what we have already,
cues.zh: 所以，当有机会大幅加速这个过程时，我们就应该抓住它。如果你同意我的看法，认为幂的三角形显然比我们现有的方式更好，

cues.en: start actually using it in your notes to see what it feels like. Spread the word. And if you're a teacher, maybe start teaching this to your students so that we can get them hooked while they're young.
cues.zh: 那就开始在笔记里实际使用它，看看感觉如何。把这个消息传播出去。如果你是老师，也许可以开始把这个教给你的学生，这样我们就能在他们还小的时候让他们产生兴趣。
